--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Parent strategy: starts C. If opponent defections >=3 and >= n/2 -> D. Tf2T: defect if opponent last two D. Endgame defect last 2. If opp_last D and my_last D, 70% D. Otherwise C. It does decent (269.88 highest among shown). We need improve."
STRATEGY: Parent starts C, retaliates when opponent defections >=3 and >= n/2, uses Tf2T (defect if opponent last two D), defects last 2 rounds, and defects 70% if both last actions were D. The trace simulates IPD payoffs and opponent types (always C, always D, TFT, Tf2T, Grim, Pavlov, random, slot 0-11) and proposes adapting/exploiting by detecting responsiveness, defecting against unconditional cooperators, cooperating until the end against retaliators, and occasionally defecting against exploiters.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "So the optimal against slot6 is to defect once every 10 rounds, getting ~2.9 average." / "So we can safely say: if opponent defects in the first round, we defect always."
STRATEGY: The parent is a Tf2T-style strategy that starts C, defects after two consecutive opponent Ds, defects when opponent defections are >=3 and >= n//2, defects in the endgame when remaining <=2, and defects 70% after mutual D. The trace simulates this parent against TFT, slot0, slot1, slot6, random, and endgame defectors, and proposes changes: defect only at the last round against cooperative opponents, detect early/frequent opponent defection, and switch to a 10-round defect pattern or always-D depending on whether the opponent is exploitative, random, or always-D.

ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / discarded the report / said the trace itself misread the probe — "Let's outline a new strategy:" and "Let's draft a strategy:" and "Let's write the final strategy cleanly."
STRATEGY: The parent is a Tf2T-like strategy with endgame defection. The trace simulates opponents including TFT, slot0, slot1, slot6, always D, and random. It changes the strategy by adding anti-exploitation mode, early defection against first-round D, endgame adjustments, and a rule to defect always if the opponent cooperates after our defection.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the rule handles both cases well." / "Overall, our strategy seems solid."
STRATEGY: Parent defects in the first round if the opponent did, defects after a D/C, defects if opponent's early defection rate is high, and defects in the endgame. Simulated against TFT, Grim, Tf2T, slot0, slot1, slot5, slot6, random, always-D. Changed by moving endgame checks before AEM, adding a static first-10-round AEM trigger, and adding an endgame override for exploitative opponents.

Simulated against slot6, TFT, slot0, random, always-D, slot2, slot5. Changed by adding an AEM endgame rule: if n >= 96, return 'D'.
